history.america-judgement.0018.all: Plan: economic (land hunger, cotton, fur, gold 1848, Louisiana Purchase for New Orleans trade) vs Manifest Destiny, security/Mexico, politics (Polk), slavery extension, transport. Texas 1845 was partly political/slavery. Judge: economics important but combined with ideology.

history.america-judgement.0019.all: Plan: Texas 1845 added land, led to Mexican War 1846-48 and Mexican Cession; but Louisiana Purchase 1803 (stimulus says 'doubled', roughly right) bigger, Oregon 1846, Mexican Cession larger, Gadsden. Texas significant as trigger of war, slavery debate; not the largest.

history.germany-effects.0010.all: 1) Kaiser abdicated, Germany became republic (Weimar). 2) Armistice 11 Nov 1918 ending war; or Spartacist/ Ebert-Groener pact, Freikorps violence, lasting divisions/stab in the back myth.

history.germany-effects.0044.all: 1) Control of information - only Nazi ideas, propaganda by Goebbels, books burned May 1933. 2) Culture: artists/writers fled or silenced; Reich Chamber of Culture; fear of criticism.

history.germany-effects.0039.all: 1) Decree for Protection of People and State suspended civil rights, KPD arrests. 2) Enabling Act in March 1933 passed, Nazis gained dictatorship; increased Nazi vote in March election (43.9%).

history.germany-effects.0005.all: 1) Passive resistance, Germany stopped reparations, economy damaged. 2) Hyperinflation 1923, savings wiped out; Stresemann called off resistance, led to Dawes Plan; fed extremism (Munich Putsch).

history.germany-effects.0017.all: 1) Reduced reparations total (to 37 billion marks over 59 years) lower annual payments. 2) Allied troops left Rhineland early 1930; nationalists (Hugenberg, Nazis) attacked it, gaining publicity.

history.germany-effects.0061.all: 1) Civilian casualties/destruction of cities (Hamburg, Dresden), homelessness, morale. 2) Disrupted industry/transport/oil, diverted resources to air defence, reduced war production; evacuation.

history.america-judgement.0019.problem: Second stimulus bullet 'It doubled the size of the country in 1803' is an unattached pronoun for the Louisiana Purchase, not Texas annexation; mark scheme treats it as the opposing factor.
history.america-judgement.0019.fix: Replace with a Texas-relevant bullet, e.g. 'It led to war with Mexico in 1846'; keep the Louisiana Purchase as an own-knowledge factor.
